title: Topological Clustering via Sliced Wasserstien Kernels
summary: Topological data analysis (TDA) uses topological techniques to extract meaningful shape-based information from complex datasets. Clustering is a central problem in data analysis, and there has been considerable recent interest in understanding how TDA can inform it. Existing approaches either cluster persistence diagrams directly under Wasserstein-type distances, which is computationally expensive, or use vector representations of diagrams. We propose a kernel $k$-means algorithm built on a convex combination of sliced Wasserstein (SW) kernels, one for each homology under consideration.…
